proposed_fix.description: Confirm network-level loss/delay on the node hosting ts-travel-service, then mitigate by gated, reversible rescheduling or capacity changes.
steps: Identify the node and pod(s) running ts-travel-service and check node NIC counters (rx/tx errors, drops) and TCP retransmits for that node.
Check conntrack usage vs. limit on that node (e.g. nf_conntrack_count vs nf_conntrack_max) and look for conntrack drop messages in the kernel log.

Compare node-level network health of the other callee nodes (ts-route-service, ts-order-service, ts-seat-service, ts-ticketinfo-service, ts-train-service) to confirm the issue is local to ts-travel-service's node.

If the node shows network errors or conntrack pressure, and with human approval, cordon the node and reschedule one ts-travel-service replica to a healthy node; watch ts-travel-service latency-50 and socket metrics.
If the replica on the healthy node recovers, proceed with remaining replicas one at a time; otherwise escalate to the node/network team for deeper investigation (firewall rules, CNI, hardware).
preconditions: Confirm ts-travel-service has more than one replica or that a brief single-replica disruption is acceptable.
Verify the target node has spare CPU/memory capacity to receive the pod.
Obtain on-call approval before cordoning or evicting anything.
Confirm the slowdown is still ongoing (E5 latency-50 still elevated) before acting.
proposed_fix.rollback: Uncordon the node and, if needed, scale or reschedule the pods back; revert any conntrack limit change to its previous value (record the original before changing anything).
